# Apple

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="apple-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="apple-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="apple-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Fresh apples are usually low in lead, with medians below reporting limits in large monitoring sets, but some regional submissions and dried apple run higher; cadmium is the metal closest to the EU pome-fruit limit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals of concern:</strong>

Lead and cadmium; arsenic and mercury are mostly below detection in fresh apple.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

The market and laboratory sampled, irrigation water, and drying, which concentrates metals.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nasirpour M, Khoshkam M, Rezaei Z, Mirzaei M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">The changes of heavy metals and some necessary elements in leaf, fruit and soil on apple cultivar golden delicious by applying urban treated wastewater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Plant Biology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot-specific lead and cadmium results on the fruit, with a quantification limit well below 20 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
</ul>
</section>

<a id="decision-summary"></a>
## Apple overview

<a id="hmi-ing-004"></a>
<a id="which-contamination-concerns-are-supported-for-this-ingredient-and-its-defined-forms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-005"></a>
<a id="which-sourcing-or-production-decisions-deserve-priority-on-the-available-evidence"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-006"></a>
<a id="which-evidence-gaps-most-limit-those-decisions"></a>

Fresh apples are usually low in lead in large monitoring datasets, but not uniformly so. In WHO GEMS/Food, the median lead result for fresh apple was below laboratory reporting limits in every large regional set, and 15 of 3,321 European results and 13 of 982 results from the Americas exceeded 100 µg/kg, the EU and Codex maximum for fruit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxs-193-1995|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Codex Alimentarius (Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Apples submitted from the Western Pacific region under random sampling were higher, with a median of about 24 µg/kg, and all 56 of the 806 regional results above 100 µg/kg were collected between 2001 and 2008.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Cadmium, arsenic and mercury in fresh apple are mostly below detection.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> All 27 FDA Total Diet Study composites of raw red apple bought in the United States in 2017–2020 were below reporting limits for lead (4 µg/kg), cadmium (1 µg/kg), mercury (1 µg/kg) and nickel (40 µg/kg), and seven had total arsenic between 3 and 20 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a <a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as apple

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers fresh apple fruit (Malus domestica) as bought or harvested: whole apples with the peel on, peeled apple flesh and apples analysed washed or unwashed, together with dried apple as a separate form.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-apple" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-apple-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of apple, group and metal. Fresh apple, peeled apple, unwashed apple and dried apple are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with fresh or as-sold results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results for the same form of apple. Same-study contrasts compare unwashed with washed apples, dried with fresh apple, wastewater-irrigated with well-water apples, or two areas of one diet study. Held rows failed a check against their own paper and are shown but not compared.</p>

data-shared-occurrence-methods><summary>Shared dataset methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:apple-fresh-fw-Pb:99c89bdb29cf"><summary>HMI apple Pb reference · Fresh apple, peel on or not stated</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:apple-fresh-fw-Pb:99c89bdb29cf"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI apple Pb reference · Fresh apple, peel on or not stated. Fresh apple, peel on or not stated; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤1</td><td>≤4</td><td>1–7 (bounded)</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤1</td><td>≤4</td><td>1–7 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>78 reference units; 3 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>72</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>FDA Total Diet Study 2018–2020</td><td>5</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Bramwell et al. 2022</td><td>1</td><td>33%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians of fresh apple, peel on or not stated on an as-sold or fresh-weight basis: individual WHO GEMS/Food results summarised per WHO region, sampling type and collection year, FDA Total Diet Study composites summarised per national collection, and published survey medians. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Peeled, unwashed and dried apple, dry-weight results and results without a stated basis are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1–Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>3 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. WHO regions are reporting regions, not growing areas. Many results are non-detects with differing limits, which widens the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" data-no-cite-meta>FDA Total Diet Study 2018–2020</a></li><li><a href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead" class="internal" data-slug="sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead" data-no-cite-meta>Bramwell et al. 2022</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:apple-fresh-fw-Pb:99c89bdb29cf</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Apple trees appear to move little lead into the fruit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lindsay Bramwell, Jane Entwistle, Jackie Morton, Anne-Helen Harding, Nan Lin · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead">Determinants of blood and saliva lead concentrations in adult gardeners on urban agricultural sites</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Geochemistry and Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> On urban allotments in Newcastle, where soils averaged 327 mg/kg lead, apples had a median of 1 µg/kg lead on a fresh-weight basis, the lowest of every crop group measured, against medians of 23 µg/kg for root vegetables and 19 µg/kg for shrub fruit such as raspberries.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lindsay Bramwell, Jane Entwistle, Jackie Morton, Anne-Helen Harding, Nan Lin · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead">Determinants of blood and saliva lead concentrations in adult gardeners on urban agricultural sites</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Geochemistry and Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Irrigation water can matter for arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nasirpour M, Khoshkam M, Rezaei Z, Mirzaei M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">The changes of heavy metals and some necessary elements in leaf, fruit and soil on apple cultivar golden delicious by applying urban treated wastewater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Plant Biology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In a Golden Delicious orchard near Mashhad, Iran, fruit from trees watered with treated municipal wastewater carried about 380–390 µg/kg arsenic on a dry-weight basis in the second year against 140–150 µg/kg with well water, while first-year results did not separate clearly (630–780 µg/kg in every treatment).<sup class="cite">[[sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nasirpour M, Khoshkam M, Rezaei Z, Mirzaei M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">The changes of heavy metals and some necessary elements in leaf, fruit and soil on apple cultivar golden delicious by applying urban treated wastewater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Plant Biology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> These values were read from a bar chart, the method was not one usually sensitive enough for arsenic, and no detection limit or reference material was reported, so the direction is more reliable than the size.<sup class="cite">[[sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nasirpour M, Khoshkam M, Rezaei Z, Mirzaei M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">The changes of heavy metals and some necessary elements in leaf, fruit and soil on apple cultivar golden delicious by applying urban treated wastewater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Plant Biology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Older orchard practices are a possible lead source that no study in the library measured directly. In the Newcastle study, eating more bought tree fruit was associated with higher blood lead in gardeners and non-gardeners alike, and the authors suggested historic lead arsenate sprays as one explanation without testing it.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lindsay Bramwell, Jane Entwistle, Jackie Morton, Anne-Helen Harding, Nan Lin · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead">Determinants of blood and saliva lead concentrations in adult gardeners on urban agricultural sites</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Geochemistry and Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

→</a></span></span></sup>

Higher lead was reported from the Western Pacific and South-East Asia regions.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Western Pacific apples under random sampling had a median of about 24 µg/kg, and 32 of 262 random-sampling results from 1998–2004 exceeded 100 µg/kg against none of 12 from 2010–2014, so this pattern belongs mostly to older submissions.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Ten apples from South-East Asia in 2012–2013 had a median of 75 µg/kg; ten results cannot represent a region.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO regions are reporting regions, not growing areas, so these are lowest observed patterns by market, not rankings of producing countries.

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-apple-variety-change-lead-or-cadmium" data-anchor="does-apple-variety-change-lead-or-cadmium" data-question="Does apple variety change lead or cadmium?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does apple variety change lead or cadmium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Not measurably in the evidence: every named cultivar submitted from the Americas in 2014–2016 had a lead median below the 5 µg/kg reporting limit, and only single results reached 63 µg/kg (McIntosh) and 43 µg/kg (Gala).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No study compared cultivars for cadmium.

</div>
</details>


<a id="processing-effects"></a>
<a id="ingredient-derivative-risk"></a>
<a id="processing-effects-and-derivatives"></a>
## Washing, peeling and drying

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>
<a id="how-do-derivatives-concentrates-extracts-and-fractions-differ-from-their-parent-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-018"></a>
<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

Washing, peeling and drying are the processing steps with apple evidence, and only drying has a clear measured effect. In a 1998 Western Pacific survey, washed and unwashed apples both had lead, cadmium, arsenic and mercury medians below reporting limits of 2.5–5 µg/kg, so washing could not be shown to lower these metals at such low levels.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No study measured peeled and unpeeled apples from the same lot; peeled apples bought in South Korea averaged 46 µg/kg lead and peeled apples on the Polish market 9 µg/kg, a difference between markets and laboratories rather than an effect of peeling.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lee2023-south-korea-fresh-fruits-seven-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lee J, Hwang I, Park YS, Lee DY · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lee2023-south-korea-fresh-fruits-seven-metals">Occurrence and health risk assessment of antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, chromium, nickel, and lead in fresh fruits consumed in South Korea</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Biological Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lee2023-south-korea-fresh-fruits-seven-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Drying concentrates metals per kilogram.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Dried apple submitted to GEMS/Food from Europe had a lead median of 26–29 µg/kg under random sampling against below 10 µg/kg for fresh apple, and on the Polish market dried apple averaged 127 µg/kg lead and 23 µg/kg cadmium on a dry-weight basis against 9 and 1 µg/kg in fresh peeled apple.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants Abbas SH, Abojassim AA · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/hadi2025-dried-fruits-heavy-metals-iraq">Health Impact of Heavy Metals in Samples of Dried Fruits in <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-peeling-an-apple-remove-lead" data-anchor="does-peeling-an-apple-remove-lead" data-question="Does peeling an apple remove lead?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does peeling an apple remove lead?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No study in the library measured peeled and unpeeled apples from the same lot, so the size of any reduction is unknown.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span difference that tracks the market and laboratory rather than peeling.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" <a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Mitigation from orchard to market

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-020"></a>
<a id="under-what-conditions-at-which-stage-and-against-which-comparator-do-they-work-or-fail"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-021"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-field-or-commercial-implementation-and-ongoing-verification"></a>

Controls for metals in apples act at the orchard, during handling and storage, and at lot release. The only measured orchard comparison is irrigation water: wastewater-irrigated Golden Delicious fruit carried more arsenic than well-water fruit in one of two years, while the choice among three rootstocks made no significant difference to fruit arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nasirpour M, Khoshkam M, Rezaei Z, Mirzaei M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">The changes of heavy metals and some necessary elements in leaf, fruit and soil on apple cultivar golden delicious by applying urban treated wastewater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Plant Biology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Siting evidence is observational: apples grown on lead-contaminated urban allotment soil still had the lowest lead of any crop measured there.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lindsay Bramwell, Jane Entwistle, Jackie Morton, Anne-Helen Harding, Nan Lin · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead">Determinants of blood and saliva lead concentrations in adult gardeners on urban agricultural sites</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Geochemistry and Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Handling controls rest on guidance and descriptive comparisons rather than tested effects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/bfr2020-aluminium-faq-consumer-products|32]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment (BfR) · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bfr2020-aluminium-faq-consumer-products">FAQs about aluminium in food and products intended for consumers</a></span><span →</a></span></span></sup> The EU defines its limits on washed fruit with the edible part separated, German risk assessors advise against wrapping cut apples or storing apple puree in aluminium foil, and washed and unwashed apples in one survey could not be told apart because both were below detection.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup Treated wastewater saves fresh water for orchards but raised fruit arsenic in one of two years in the only apple study, and the authors still recommended diluted or alternating use.<sup class="cite">[[sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nasirpour M, Khoshkam M, Rezaei Z, Mirzaei M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">The changes of heavy metals and some necessary elements in leaf, fruit and soil on apple cultivar golden delicious by applying urban treated wastewater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Plant Biology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Its rootstock comparison found that rootstocks changed lead and nickel in the leaves without any fruit measurement for those metals, so a rootstock chosen for one metal cannot be assumed neutral for others.<sup class="cite">[[sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nasirpour M, Khoshkam M, Rezaei Z, Mirzaei M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">The changes of heavy metals and some necessary elements in leaf, fruit and soil on apple cultivar golden delicious by applying urban treated wastewater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Plant Biology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Peeling may remove surface soil along with part of the fruit, but no study in the library measured how much lead or cadmium peeling removes from apples. Drying turns a low fresh concentration into a higher dried one, so a dried-apple result must be read against a dried-fruit limit, such as China’s 0.5 mg/kg for lead, rather than the 0.10 mg/kg Fresh apple is widely eaten by children and adults, but no source in the library estimated lead or cadmium exposure from fresh apples with verified concentrations. In total diet studies, apple was below detection for lead, cadmium and mercury in the United States and averaged 11 µg/kg lead and 6 µg/kg inorganic arsenic as eaten in Hong Kong.<sup <a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Apple FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-apples" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-apples" data-question="What heavy metals are found in apples?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in apples?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Lead is the metal most often detected in fresh apples, usually at a few micrograms per kilogram; cadmium, arsenic and mercury are mostly below detection.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Aluminium occurs at higher levels, around 380 µg/kg in Hong Kong retail apples and a median of 930 µg/kg in 16 European results.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety (Hong Kong) · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Metallic Contaminants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-apples" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-apples" data-question="How do heavy metals get into apples?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into apples?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

From orchard soil and irrigation water through the tree, and from soil and dust on the skin.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nasirpour M, Khoshkam M, Rezaei Z, Mirzaei M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">The changes of heavy metals and some necessary elements in leaf, fruit and soil on apple cultivar golden delicious by applying urban treated wastewater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Plant Biology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Apple trees move little lead into the fruit: apples on lead-contaminated allotment soil had a median of 1 µg/kg lead, the lowest of every crop measured there.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lindsay Bramwell, Jane Entwistle, Jackie Morton, Anne-Helen Harding, Nan Lin · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead">Determinants of blood and saliva lead concentrations in adult gardeners on urban agricultural sites</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Geochemistry and Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-organic-apples-lower-in-heavy-metals" data-anchor="are-organic-apples-lower-in-heavy-metals" data-question="Are organic apples lower in heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are organic apples lower in heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Not measurably: apples labelled organic in GEMS/Food submissions from the Americas had a lead median of 1–2 µg/kg against no more than 2.2 µg/kg for other apples, and inorganic arsenic was below detection in organic and conventional apples alike in the FDA 2016 survey.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic">Analytical Results from Inorganic Arsenic in Rice Cereals for Infants, Non-Rice Infant Cereal and Other Foods Commonly Eaten by Infants and Toddlers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Food and Drug Administration</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> An organic label describes how the fruit was grown, not a test result for metals.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-apple-varieties-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-apple-varieties-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which apple varieties have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which apple varieties have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

None can be named: every cultivar submitted from the Americas in 2014–2016, including Gala, McIntosh, Red Delicious, Golden Delicious and Granny Smith, had a lead median below the 5 µg/kg reporting limit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In the FDA 2016 survey, inorganic arsenic was below detection in all nine named varieties tested.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic">Analytical Results from Inorganic Arsenic in Rice Cereals for Infants, Non-Rice Infant Cereal and Other Foods Commonly Eaten by Infants and Toddlers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Food and Drug Administration</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-countries-or-regions-produce-apples-with-the-lowest-lead" data-anchor="which-countries-or-regions-produce-apples-with-the-lowest-lead" data-question="Which countries or regions produce apples with the lowest lead?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which countries or regions produce apples with the lowest lead?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Apples reported from the Americas and the United States were lowest: a GEMS/Food median at or below 2.1 µg/kg and all 27 US Total Diet Study composites below 4 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> These are reporting markets, not growing areas, so the evidence cannot name the producing countries with the lowest lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-foods-made-from-apples-also-contain-heavy-metals" data-anchor="do-foods-made-from-apples-also-contain-heavy-metals" data-question="Do foods made from apples also contain heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do foods made from apples also contain heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Dried apple carries more per kilogram because water is removed: European dried apple had a lead median of 26–29 µg/kg against below 10 µg/kg for fresh.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Apple juice and applesauce are covered on their own pages and are not compared here.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-do-the-levels-in-apples-mean-for-health" data-anchor="what-do-the-levels-in-apples-mean-for-health" data-question="What do the levels in apples mean for health?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What do the levels in apples mean for health?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No source in the library estimated how much lead or cadmium people take in from fresh apples, so the evidence cannot say what share of intake apples supply. Measured fresh-apple levels are mostly below the limits set for fruit, but a concentration below a limit is not by itself a measure of individual risk.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-apples" data-anchor="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-apples" data-question="Are there legal limits for heavy metals in apples?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are there legal limits for heavy metals in apples?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes: the EU sets 0.10 mg/kg lead for fruit and 0.020 mg/kg cadmium for pome fruit, Codex 0.1 mg/kg lead for fruits, and China 0.1 mg/kg lead and 0.05 mg/kg cadmium for fresh fruit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxs-193-1995|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Codex Alimentarius (Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/chinanhc2025-gb-2762-contaminants|33]]<span class="cite-card"><span
