<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-washing-apples-remove-heavy-metals" data-anchor="does-washing-apples-remove-heavy-metals" data-question="Does washing apples remove heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does washing apples remove heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Washing removes soil and dust from the skin, and the EU applies its limits to washed fruit, but the only apple comparison could not show an effect because washed and unwashed apples were both below detection.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-peeling-apples-lower-heavy-metals" data-anchor="does-peeling-apples-lower-heavy-metals" data-question="Does peeling apples lower heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does peeling apples lower heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Unknown for apples: no study in the library measured peeled and unpeeled fruit from the same lot.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lee2023-south-korea-fresh-fruits-seven-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lee J, Hwang I, Park YS, Lee DY · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lee2023-south-korea-fresh-fruits-seven-metals">Occurrence and health risk assessment of antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, chromium, nickel, and lead in fresh fruits consumed in South Korea</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Biological Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lee2023-south-korea-fresh-fruits-seven-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Peeled apples bought in South Korea and Poland averaged 46 and 9 µg/kg lead, a difference between markets rather than an effect of peeling.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lee2023-south-korea-fresh-fruits-seven-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lee J, Hwang I, Park YS, Lee DY · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lee2023-south-korea-fresh-fruits-seven-metals">Occurrence and health risk assessment of antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, chromium, nickel, and lead in fresh fruits consumed in South Korea</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Biological Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lee2023-south-korea-fresh-fruits-seven-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-the-arsenic-in-apples-the-more-toxic-inorganic-form" data-anchor="is-the-arsenic-in-apples-the-more-toxic-inorganic-form" data-question="Is the arsenic in apples the more toxic inorganic form?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is the arsenic in apples the more toxic inorganic form?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Where it was measured, inorganic arsenic in apples was low: below 2.2 µg/kg in all ten US-bought apples in the FDA 2016 survey and an average of 6 µg/kg in Hong Kong retail apples.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic">Analytical Results from Inorganic Arsenic in Rice Cereals for Infants, Non-Rice Infant Cereal and Other Foods Commonly Eaten by Infants and Toddlers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Food and Drug Administration</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety FEHD HKSAR · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Inorganic Arsenic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Most apple arsenic results are total arsenic, which includes less toxic organic forms, and fewer than 30 inorganic arsenic results exist.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic">Analytical Results from Inorganic Arsenic in Rice Cereals for Infants, Non-Rice Infant Cereal and Other Foods Commonly Eaten by Infants and Toddlers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Food and Drug Administration</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-apples-a-concern-for-babies-and-children" data-anchor="are-apples-a-concern-for-babies-and-children" data-question="Are apples a concern for babies and children?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are apples a concern for babies and children?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Fresh apple itself measured low in the studies here, but the 2023 lead poisoning cluster linked to apple-cinnamon fruit puree pouches was traced to the cinnamon, not the apples.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Napier MD, et al. · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon">Childhood Lead Exposure Linked to Apple Cinnamon Fruit Puree Pouches — North Carolina, June 2023–January 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Apple juice and apple baby foods are covered on their own pages.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-dried-apple-higher-in-heavy-metals-than-fresh-apple" data-anchor="is-dried-apple-higher-in-heavy-metals-than-fresh-apple" data-question="Is dried apple higher in heavy metals than fresh apple?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is dried apple higher in heavy metals than fresh apple?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Per kilogram, yes, because drying removes most of the water: on the Polish market dried apple averaged 127 µg/kg lead and 23 µg/kg cadmium on a dry-weight basis against 9 and 1 µg/kg in fresh peeled apple.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Single dried products from Iraq and Iran reported up to 897 µg/kg cadmium on an unstated basis, so dried apple is worth testing as dried product.<sup class="cite">[[sources/hadi2025-dried-fruits-heavy-metals-iraq|17]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Hadi QM, Mahdi FA, Hamood FJ, Abbas SH, Abojassim AA · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/hadi2025-dried-fruits-heavy-metals-iraq">Health Impact of Heavy Metals in Samples of Dried Fruits in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Analytical Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/hadi2025-dried-fruits-heavy-metals-iraq">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/mahmood2025-dried-fruit-metals|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mahmood BA, Alkubaisy SA, Marouf EAAK, Mohammed EH · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mahmood2025-dried-fruit-metals">Estimation of some heavy metal concentrations in selected dried fruit samples available in local markets and assessment of their health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Environmental Impacts</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mahmood2025-dried-fruit-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-apples-from-orchards-irrigated-with-wastewater-carry-more-arsenic" data-anchor="do-apples-from-orchards-irrigated-with-wastewater-carry-more-arsenic" data-question="Do apples from orchards irrigated with wastewater carry more arsenic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do apples from orchards irrigated with wastewater carry more arsenic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the one apple study, yes in the second year: Golden Delicious fruit watered with treated wastewater carried about 380–390 µg/kg arsenic on a dry-weight basis against 140–150 µg/kg with well water.<sup class="cite">[[sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nasirpour M, Khoshkam M, Rezaei Z, Mirzaei M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">The changes of heavy metals and some necessary elements in leaf, fruit and soil on apple cultivar golden delicious by applying urban treated wastewater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Plant Biology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> First-year results did not separate clearly, and the values were read from a chart without a reported detection limit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nasirpour M, Khoshkam M, Rezaei Z, Mirzaei M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">The changes of heavy metals and some necessary elements in leaf, fruit and soil on apple cultivar golden delicious by applying urban treated wastewater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Plant Biology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-apples-grown-in-urban-gardens-high-in-lead" data-anchor="are-apples-grown-in-urban-gardens-high-in-lead" data-question="Are apples grown in urban gardens high in lead?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are apples grown in urban gardens high in lead?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Not in the evidence available: on Newcastle allotments with soil averaging 327 mg/kg lead, apples had a median of 1 µg/kg lead, lower than every other crop measured.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lindsay Bramwell, Jane Entwistle, Jackie Morton, Anne-Helen Harding, Nan Lin · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead">Determinants of blood and saliva lead concentrations in adult gardeners on urban agricultural sites</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Geochemistry and Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Root vegetables and soft fruit from the same sites were much higher, so the crop matters more than the site for apples.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lindsay Bramwell, Jane Entwistle, Jackie Morton, Anne-Helen Harding, Nan Lin · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead">Determinants of blood and saliva lead concentrations in adult gardeners on urban agricultural sites</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Geochemistry and Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bramwell2022-urban-garden-produce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-imported-apples-higher-in-lead-than-locally-grown-ones" data-anchor="are-imported-apples-higher-in-lead-than-locally-grown-ones" data-question="Are imported apples higher in lead than locally grown ones?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are imported apples higher in lead than locally grown ones?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In European monitoring the opposite held in the high tail: none of 1,222 apples labelled imported exceeded 100 µg/kg lead against 14 of 1,875 labelled domestic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The share above 50 µg/kg was similar, and the export does not name the country of growth.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="has-lead-in-apples-been-falling" data-anchor="has-lead-in-apples-been-falling" data-question="Has lead in apples been falling?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Has lead in apples been falling?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In Western Pacific submissions it fell: 32 of 262 random-sampling results from 1998–2004 exceeded 100 µg/kg against none of 12 from 2010–2014.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In Europe the median stayed below 10 µg/kg from 2000 to 2020, with fewer than 1% of results above 100 µg/kg in each period.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-can-i-tell-whether-an-apple-metals-test-is-good-enough" data-anchor="how-can-i-tell-whether-an-apple-metals-test-is-good-enough" data-question="How can I tell whether an apple metals test is good enough?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How can I tell whether an apple metals test is good enough?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Check that the quantification limit is far below the limit being checked: under 20 µg/kg for cadmium and well under 100 µg/kg for lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Laboratories reporting apples from the Americas used lead limits of 1–5 µg/kg, while some European non-detects had limits of 100 µg/kg or more, which cannot show compliance.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="can-aluminium-foil-add-aluminium-to-cut-apples" data-anchor="can-aluminium-foil-add-aluminium-to-cut-apples" data-question="Can aluminium foil add aluminium to cut apples?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Can aluminium foil add aluminium to cut apples?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

German risk assessors advise against wrapping cut apples or storing apple puree in aluminium foil or uncoated aluminium, because acidic foods take up aluminium from it.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bfr2020-aluminium-faq-consumer-products|32]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment (BfR) · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bfr2020-aluminium-faq-consumer-products">FAQs about aluminium in food and products intended for consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BfR FAQ of 20 July 2020</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bfr2020-aluminium-faq-consumer-products">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The advice is qualitative; no apple measurement is given.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bfr2020-aluminium-faq-consumer-products|32]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment (BfR) · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bfr2020-aluminium-faq-consumer-products">FAQs about aluminium in food and products intended for consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BfR FAQ of 20 July 2020</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bfr2020-aluminium-faq-consumer-products">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="why-do-some-studies-report-much-higher-heavy-metals-in-apples" data-anchor="why-do-some-studies-report-much-higher-heavy-metals-in-apples" data-question="Why do some studies report much higher heavy metals in apples?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Why do some studies report much higher heavy metals in apples?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Mostly because of basis and method: dry-weight results are several times fresh-weight ones, and several market surveys printed values below their own detection limits or implausibly high across every food tested.<sup class="cite">[[sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nasirpour M, Khoshkam M, Rezaei Z, Mirzaei M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">The changes of heavy metals and some necessary elements in leaf, fruit and soil on apple cultivar golden delicious by applying urban treated wastewater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Plant Biology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nasirpour2026-apple-wastewater-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/afrin2020-heavy-metals-fruits-dhaka|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Afrin S · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/afrin2020-heavy-metals-fruits-dhaka">Determination and Risk Analysis of Heavy Metals in Different Fruits Collected from Different Shops of Dhaka City</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">M.S. Thesis, Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University, Dhaka</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/afrin2020-heavy-metals-fruits-dhaka">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/rahim2020-toxic-heavy-metals-fruits-pakistan|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rahim M, Saqib NU, Wahid F, Khan N, Alrawi
